appaccess.title: Programs
appaccess.intro: Who sees and may open which Docker app on the desktop. Without a tick the app is also locked at its address in the browser.
appaccess.adminAlways: Owners and administrators may always use every app; their ticks cannot be cleared.
appaccess.gate: Check the login in the browser
appaccess.gateFor: Check the login in the browser for {app}
appaccess.gateHint: Page loads in a browser then need the TitanOS login and the right to the app. Apps on phones and TVs that only use the app's API (e.g. the Immich or Bitwarden app) keep signing in on their own and are not affected. Apps that show the app's web page (e.g. the Jellyfin app for Android or the Home Assistant app) are locked out at the HTTPS name: switch the check off for that app or connect them through the app's port.
appaccess.gateLimit: The lock guards the app's pages in the browser. Its API stays guarded by the app's own login.
appaccess.newAppsHint: Who gets a newly installed app right away.
appaccess.noUsers: There are only owners and administrators, and they may use every app. Add normal users under Users.
appaccess.noNameHint: Apps without an HTTPS name do not open in a window. Switch on the automatic names under “HTTPS names for apps” or give the app a name of its own.
appaccess.autoNames: Automatically for all apps with a WebUI
appaccess.autoNamesHint: Every Docker app with a WebUI gets an HTTPS name of its own (home network only), so that it opens in a window on the desktop. An app's own settings come first; switching off or editing an automatic name makes it the app's own.
appaccess.caIntro: Without a certificate from Let's Encrypt or Tailscale, TitanOS issues the certificates of its own addresses and of the HTTPS names itself. Install the certificate authority once on every device: browsers then stop warning, and apps open in windows too.
appaccess.caNotNeeded: With Let's Encrypt (own domain or IPv64) or a Tailscale name nothing needs to be installed.
appaccess.caUnavailable: The certificate authority is not available right now. Can the stick be read?
appaccess.caWindows: Open the .crt file › “Install Certificate” › “Local Machine” › “Place all certificates in the following store” › “Trusted Root Certification Authorities”. Restart Firefox afterwards.
appaccess.caMac: Open the .crt file; Keychain Access adds it to the “System” keychain. Double-click the TitanOS certificate authority › “Trust” › “When using this certificate”: “Always Trust”.
appaccess.caIos: Load the .crt file in Safari and allow it › Settings › “Profile Downloaded” › Install. Then switch on full trust for the TitanOS certificate authority under Settings › General › About › Certificate Trust Settings.
appaccess.caAndroid: Download the .crt file › Settings › Security › More security settings › Encryption & credentials › Install a certificate › CA certificate. Menu names differ between makers.
appaccess.caLinux: Copy the .crt file to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ and run “sudo update-ca-certificates”. Firefox and Chromium keep lists of their own: import it there under Settings › Certificates › Authorities.
appaccess.caKey: The private key stays on the stick in /config. TitanOS never hands it out, not even in the diagnostic bundle.
appaccess.certCa: Issued by the TitanOS certificate authority. Once it is installed on your device, the browser does not warn.
